'''Fernand Seguin'''  (June 9, 1922 &ndash; June 19, 1988) was a [[Canadians|Canadian]] [[biochemist]], professor and host of science programs on radio and television.  

Seguin, who hosted a program on Radio-Canada's TV network in 1954, is believed{{by whom?|date=September 2026}} to be the first broadcaster to present a science program on television in Canada.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2018-06-20 |first1=Zone Science - |language=fr-ca |last1=ICI.Radio-Canada.ca |title=Fernand Seguin, le savant de Radio-Canada |url=https://ici.radio-canada.ca/nouvelle/1107069/fernand-seguin-biographie-carriere-journaliste-animateur-emission-scientifique-archives |website=Radio-Canada.ca}}<!-- auto-translated from French by Module:CS1 translator -->.</ref>

He was the first Canadian to receive the UNESCO [[Kalinga Prize]] for the Popularization of Science, the only other being David Suzuki in 1986. His nomination was advanced as the inaugural act of {{lang|fr|l’Association des communicateurs scientifiques du Québec}} (ACS).

==Honours==
* 1952 – co-winner of a Canadian Radio Award from the Canadian Association for Adult Education for his radio programme {{lang|fr|Carte blanche}} in the "light entertainment" category.<ref>[https://numerique.banq.qc.ca/patrimoine/details/52327/3542391?docsearchtext=canadian "André Roche gagne un 'Canadian Radio Award{{' "}}], ''Photo-journal'' (Montréal), Nov 13, 1952, p. 3. (Accessed Jan 9, 2026.)</ref>
* 1961 – {{lang|fr|Médaille Archambault}} (medal) from {{lang|fr|l’Association canadienne-française pour l’avancement des sciences}} (French-Canadian Association for the Advancement of Science) for his writings and films that popularized science topics. The medal was "presented annually for works of outstanding practical merit by French-speaking scientists".<ref>[https://numerique.banq.qc.ca/patrimoine/details/52327/2756758?docsearchtext=seguin "Médaille de l'ACFAS"], ''La Presse'' (Montréal), Oct 30, 1961, p. 9. (Accessed Dec 30, 2025.)</ref><ref>"Montreal Man Elected Head of Scientists", ''The Gazette'' (Montréal), p. 4.</ref>
* 1968 – co-winner of the {{lang|fr|Prix Mandarine}} for his interview television programme {{lang|fr|Le Sel de la semaine}}.<ref>[https://numerique.banq.qc.ca/patrimoine/details/52327/2882350?docsearchtext=Mandarine "Regardez bien, regardez 'Le Sel de la semaine': tel est le verdict des responsables des prix Mandarine et Eclair"], ''Ici Radio-Canada'' (Montréal), Apr 6, 1968, p. 20 (Accessed Jan 9, 2026.).</ref><ref>[https://numerique.banq.qc.ca/patrimoine/details/52327/3100073?docsearchtext=Mandarine "Artistes, télévision et commerciaux jugés par les journalistes: Voici les récipiendaires des prix: ...],  ''Télé-radiomonde'' (Montréal), Apr 6, 1968, p. 13. (Accessed Jan 9, 2026.) </ref><ref>[https://numerique.banq.qc.ca/patrimoine/details/52327/3099446?docsearchtext=prix "Les Prix Orange et Citron seront attribués sous peu à la télévision"], ''Télé-radiomonde'' (Montréal), Feb 27, 1965, p. 3. (Accessed Jan 9, 2026.)</ref>
* 1968 – {{lang|fr|Trophée "Méritas"}} (award) for best television interviewer, as determined by a vote of readers of the newspapers and magazines of {{lang|fr|Publications Péladeau}}.<ref>Bernard Dubé, "Radio and Television: ... French Artists Honored", ''The Gazette'' (Montréal), Jun 6, 1968, p. 28.</ref><ref>[https://numerique.banq.qc.ca/patrimoine/details/52327/3100120?docsearchtext=intervieweur  "La course aux Méritas"], ''Télé-radiomonde'' (Montréal), Jun 8, 1968, pp. 32-34; and "600 artistes arrivent à leur Gala!", pp. 10-14. (Accessed Jan 9, 2026.)</ref><ref>[https://numerique.banq.qc.ca/patrimoine/details/52327/3099795?docsearchtext=artistes  "Le prochain Gala des Artistes"], ''Télé-radiomonde'' (Montréal), Jan 7, 1967, p. 3. (Accessed Jan 9, 2026.)</ref>
* 1975 – Honorary doctorate from {{lang|fr|[[Université de Sherbrooke]]}}.<ref>[https://numerique.banq.qc.ca/patrimoine/details/52327/2944454?docsearchtext=fernand "University called essential for forming Quebec culture"], ''Sherbrooke Record'', Jun 9, 1975, p. 3. (Accessed Dec 30, 1975.)</ref>
* 1977 – {{lang|fr|Prix de journalisme Olivar-Asselin}} (journalism award) from {{lang|fr|La Société Saint-Jean-Baptiste de Montréal}} "for his work in making scientific matters understandable to the public."<ref>[https://numerique.banq.qc.ca/patrimoine/details/52327/2775794?docsearchtext=Olivar-Asselin "Le prix Olivar-Asselin est décerné à Fernand Séguin"], ''Le Devoir'' (Montréal), Oct 25, 1977, p. 23.</ref><ref>"Librarian honored", ''Montreal Star'', Nov 2, 1977, p. * 1985 – Officer of the [[National Order of Quebec]].<ref>[https://numerique.banq.qc.ca/patrimoine/details/52327/2251419?docsearchtext=%22fernand%20seguin%22 "Les premiers titulaires de l'Ordre du Québec"], ''La Presse'' (Montréal), Jun 26, 1985, p. B1. (Accessed Dec 30, 2025.)</ref>

(Accessed Jan 5, 2025.)</ref> 
* 1988 – {{lang|fr|École Fernand-Seguin}} (primary school) in [[Montréal]] was named in his honour.<ref> [https://numerique.banq.qc.ca/patrimoine/details/52327/2260423?docsearchtext=cécm "Une école de la CÉCM portera le nom de Fernand Seguin"], ''La Presse'' (Montréal), Sep 14, 1988, p.
